messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: reserved-pool-3 GPU utilization > 98% (threshold 90%) for 6m, queue growth detected, affected tenants: CedarOne, LumenPay. Paging rotation: luke (oncall)

luke (oncall): looking now. digging into queue metrics — are we seeing a noisy tenant or genuine traffic spike? :eyes:

anya (sre): I see long tail in live-queue for resv-3, most sessions show high token-per-request. Could be model runaway or batch size misconfig on tenant side.

nora (runtime): autoscaler logs show multiple scale_up attempts rejected at max_pool_capacity. max_count=12 current=12.

kevin (eng): fwiw resv-3 is pinned to A100s, we hit reservation cap earlier this morning when we merged the new batcher change. rolling back?

luke (oncall): customer-impact check — amy, any CS reports?

amy-cs: CedarOne reported higher error rates and request timeouts ~10:18-10:34 UTC. They see timeouts on realtime scoring endpoints. LumenPay on backoff but not yet routed to support.

nora (runtime): paste of autoscaler snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:20:12Z autoscaler ERROR scale_up_rejected pool=resv-3 reason=max_capacity_reached current=12 max=12
2026-03-15T10:21:05Z batcher WARN pending_queue=420 avg_wait_ms=780
```

anya (sre): queue length graph: pending spikes correlate with a handful of sessions from CedarOne holding long-lived KV cache contexts. looks like noisy session affinity.

luke (oncall): mitigation plan options: 1) evict top noisy sessions from resv-3, 2) temporarily increase pool max (if infra allows), 3) move affected tenants to fallback pool (resv-5) with warmup. Which is fastest?

kevin (eng): fastest is eviction + soft-throttle by tenant. We can run eviction & rate-limit for CedarOne while infra investigates increasing cap (provably slower, needs approvals).

infra-bot: infra change request created: CHG-12944 increase-resv-3-capacity -> requires infra-lead approval. ETA ~ 25m.

nora (runtime): I can run an incremental eviction targeting sessions with >50k tokens in last 3m. Command: `redwoodctl sessions list --pool resv-3 --sort=token_usage --limit=50` then `redwoodctl sessions evict --session-id <id>`

luke (oncall): go ahead nora. annotate customer-impact and reason=noisy-session-eviction. tag amy for customer comms.

nora (runtime): running list now, top offenders: sess-7f4c, sess-92ab, sess-a12f (CedarOne) — issuing eviction.

nora (runtime): evict commands executed:
```
redwoodctl sessions evict --session-id sess-7f4c --pool resv-3 --reason "noisy session eviction" --force
redwoodctl sessions evict --session-id sess-92ab --pool resv-3 --reason "noisy session eviction" --force
```

luke (oncall): monitoring queue and customer errors. amy, let CedarOne know we are doing targeted evictions to restore latency.

amy-cs: on it — sending message now. will keep them updated. :mailbox_with_mail:

nora (runtime): queue down from 420 -> 180 pending in 3m, avg_wait_ms 780 -> 260. autoscaler still at max but pressure reduced.

anya (sre): still seeing a small group of sessions slowly growing. recommend applying tenant rate-limit policy to CedarOne for next 30m to prevent re-entry while infra escalates capacity.

kevin (eng): I can push a tenant-level throttling override in the routing layer: `routectl set-rate cedarone 10rps` — will that work?

luke (oncall): authorize. do it and confirm.

kevin (eng): applied: cedarone -> 12rps. routing reports active sessions drop by 40% within 60s.

amy-cs: CedarOne acknowledged — they saw immediate improvement. thanks.

infra-bot: CHG-12944 approved by infra-lead, provisioning additional node-slot to resv-3, but host allocation takes ~14m.

nora (runtime): good to know. keep eviction + throttling in place until new capacity comes up. I'll also enable prefix KV cache eviction for noisy sessions to free KV memory: `runtimectl kv-evict --pool resv-3 --selector "token_usage>20000"`

luke (oncall): that's a good defensive move. any sign of other tenants being impacted?

anya (sre): LumenPay had transient slowdowns but not timeouts. No other enterprise tenants report errors so far.

kevin (eng): follow-up: we discovered a recent batcher change increased eager-padding behavior for long-context sessions, amplifying token churn. rolling that config back in next 1h unless tests fail.

luke (oncall): make sure we capture rollback instructions in the incident timeline. we'll want a postmortem.

nora (runtime): infra reports new slot attached to resv-3. autoscaler scaled to 13, pending queue fell to 40. Latency back to normal.

incident-bot: Incident severity update: SEV3 -> SEV4, customer-impact reduced. Postmortem requested.

amy-cs: CedarOne confirmed degraded window 10:17–10:34 UTC, no data lost, most requests succeeded after retries. Logging this for support ticket.

luke (oncall): prepping handoff to nighttime oncall — summary: noisy long-lived sessions from CedarOne caused reserved pool saturation; autoscaler hit max cap; mitigations: targeted session evictions, tenant rate-limiting (12rps), KV cache eviction, infra increased pool capacity + rollback of batcher change pending.

luke (oncall): @anya please own the blameless postmortem (timeline + root cause + remediation). @kevin please include the batcher rollback plan. @nora please include runbook gap for noisy session detection + auto-eviction.

anya (sre): I got it. I'll start a draft and ping for reviewers.

kevin (eng): I'll draft rollback PR and a config flag to prevent eager-padding on long-context tenants.

nora (runtime): I'll add an alert: reserved-pool pending_queue > 200 for 3m -> auto-evict top-10 sessions and notify oncall. PR coming.

luke (oncall): closing active mitigation. will update incident channel with final notes after postmortem. great work team. :clap:
